08 Frequently Asked Questions

Who is Manda and what’s the Coragem Final Tour? Manda (Amanda) is a Brazilian cantora and multi-instrumentista with a self-produced authorial catalogue. Her 2021 album “Música” passed 1 million Spotify streams; her late-2023 single “Coragem” became a viral phenomenon with over 30 million views in Instagram Reels format, six-plus months of heavy rotation on Rádio JB FM, and an extended live cycle. The “Coragem Final Tour” is the explicit closing run of that touring cycle, with São Paulo on May 17 sitting among the final dates. Manda’s live format puts her alone on stage rotating between violão, guitar, piano and baixo with band behind, mixing authorial work with releituras spanning Djavan to Lauryn Hill. Tickets via Eventim; Blue Note SP at Av. Paulista 2073, 19h single Sunday session. Who is Anaïs Sylla? Anaïs Sylla is a Paris-born singer-songwriter of Senegalese descent, based in São Paulo since 2015. She came to Brazil in 2013 to study miscigenação and the history of slavery at USP and has built a career as both historian and musician. Her music crosses West African (Mali, Senegal) and Caribean (Haiti, Martinica) sources with French chanson references (Serge Gainsbourg, Jacques Brel, Henri Salvador) and Brazilian song. She has released an EP and an authorial single “De Bouche à Bouche”, with her first full album in development. Tonight’s show at Bona Casa de Música on Sunday May 17, 2026 at 20h is part of the casa’s curated São Paulo cycle; R. Dr. Paulo Vieira 101 in Sumaré, three minutes from Metro Vila Madalena. Is Bona Casa de Música open on Sunday May 17? Yes. Bona Casa de Música at R. Dr. Paulo Vieira 101 in Sumaré reopens Sunday May 17, 2026 with Anaïs Sylla at 20h. World.title: Rio de Janeiro Nightlife Guide for Sunday, May 17, 2026
World.content:
01 Tonight's Vibe Menu

—The mood. A quiet Sunday with one ticketed headline show and three historic samba rodas. —Main ticket. Amy Reggaehouse with Clariana Fróes at Blue Note Rio, 19h, Copacabana. —Free samba. Pedra do Sal from 18h, Bip Bip from 19h, and Cacique de Ramos in Olaria from 17h. —Weather. 28 °C, partly sunny, 15 % rain. This is the warm dry night before rain returns Monday.

02 If You Only Do One Thing

—Best plan. Pedra do Sal at 18h, then Amy Reggaehouse at Blue Note Rio at 19h. —Why. You get one free historic roda and the only marquee booking of the night. —If you choose one. Pick Amy Reggaehouse if you want the rare show. Pick Pedra do Sal or Bip Bip if the budget is zero. —Do not overthink it. This is a warm Sunday. Keep the route simple and stay near Copacabana or Saúde.

03 Top Picks Tonight

Amy Reggaehouse — Clariana Fróes at Blue Note Rio 19h · Av. Atlântica 1910 · Copacabana · Ticketed —Why go. Amy Winehouse songs rebuilt through reggae, soul, jazz and Brazilian music. —Best for. The polished Sunday choice and the only big ticket of the night. —When. Doors around 18h, show at 19h, single Sunday session. —Where. Blue Note Rio, Av. Atlântica 1910, five minutes from Metro Cardeal Arcoverde. —Tip. Works well after one hour at Pedra do Sal, then a short ride to Copacabana.

Pedra do Sal — Sunday Roda From 18h · Saúde · Free · Cash —Why go. The foundational outdoor samba address on the Saúde cobblestones. —Best for. A warm evening, local atmosphere and zero-entry-cost plan. —When. From 18h until around midnight. Sunday is busy, but Monday is the legendary peak. —Where. Largo João da Baiana / R. Argemiro Bulcão. Metro Uruguaiana plus VLT, or ride-hailing. —Tip. Bring small bills. Stay with the crowd and ride back after the music.

Bip Bip — Sunday Samba in Copacabana 19h · R. Almirante Gonçalves 50 · Free · Cash —Why go. Tiny 1968 boteco, serious listening room, canonical Copacabana samba. —Best for. People already staying in Copacabana or leaving Blue Note later. —When. Sunday samba from 19h. Arrive early if you want any space. —Where. Two minutes from Metro Cardeal Arcoverde and 15 minutes on foot from Blue Note. —Tip. It is not a shouting bar. Listen, drink, keep it respectful.

Cacique de Ramos — Sunday Roda in Olaria 17h roda · 13h feijoada · R. Uranos 1326 —Why go. The Zona Norte samba temple linked to Zeca Pagodinho, Beth Carvalho, Arlindo Cruz and Jorge Aragão. —Best for. The deepest samba-history plan of the day. —When. Feijoada from 13h on the third Sunday; roda from 17h. —Where. Olaria, no metro adjacent. Count about 25 minutes by ride-hailing from Zona Sul. —Tip. This is the long-route choice. Go early or skip it if you want an easy Copacabana night.

04 Suggested Route

—Pedra do Sal into Amy Reggaehouse. Beach until 16h. Ride to Pedra do Sal by 17h30. Spend one hour on the cobblestones, then ride to Copacabana by 18h45, about 12 minutes / R$25. Amy Reggaehouse starts at 19h at Blue Note Rio. Out by 21h30, with time for dinner on Av. Atlântica. The hybrid plan: one free historic roda plus one ticketed marquee. —The two-cobblestones Sunday. Cacique de Ramos Feijoada in Olaria from 14h. Because this is the third Sunday of the month, it means free feijoada plus roda from 17h. Ride back to Centro by 19h30, then Pedra do Sal from 20h. Two foundational samba addresses in one Sunday, about R$80 in rides, free entry both. —The Copacabana Sunday. Beach until 16h. Dinner on Av. Atlântica from 17h30. Amy Reggaehouse at Blue Note Rio at 19h. Walk 15 minutes to Bip Bip for the Sunday samba roda from 21h30. Two Copacabana venues, two genres, no transport beyond the metro stop pair. —The free Sunday. Skip the ticket. Pedra do Sal from 18h, then ride to Bip Bip Copacabana by 21h for samba. Total spend: about R$40 in rides plus drinks. The local plan.

05 Still Going After 10 pm

—Note. —Note. — —Pedra do Sal. The Sunday roda winds down on the cobblestones and usually stops around midnight. —Note. — —Bip Bip. The Sunday samba roda is still in its late stretch after 22h. It is small, crowded, cash-based and best for listening, not shouting. —Note. — —Cacique de Ramos. The Olaria roda closes earlier, usually around 22h–23h. —Note. — —Rio Scenarium. Closed Sunday. The casa runs Wednesday to Saturday only. —Note. — —Carioca da Gema. Typically closed Sunday. —Note. — —Beco do Rato. R. Joaquim Silva, Lapa. Sunday hours are 12h–21h, because the casa opens early for feijoada and closes by 21h. —Note. —Circo Voador and Vivo Rio. Both are dark Sunday. Vivo Rio is dark after last night’s Emicida show. —Note. — —Blue Note Rio. The piano bar and calçadão continue after Amy Reggaehouse. The casa stays open with free piano programming on the open-air boardwalk. —Note. — —Tomorrow. Monday May 18 brings the cooling pattern: 26 °C and 50 % rain. Pedra do Sal Monday is the legendary roda night, but rain may dampen attendance. Bip Bip is closed Monday. —Note.

06 Getting Around

—Note. —Note. — —Blue Note Rio. Av. Atlântica 1910, Copacabana. Metro Cardeal Arcoverde, Yellow Line 1, five minutes on foot. —Note. — —Bip Bip. R. Almirante Gonçalves 50, Copacabana. Two minutes from Metro Cardeal Arcoverde and about 15 minutes on foot from Blue Note Rio. —Note. — —Pedra do Sal. R. Argemiro Bulcão / Largo João da Baiana, Saúde. Use Metro Uruguaiana plus VLT to Parada dos Museus, then walk five minutes. From Copacabana, a direct ride is about 12 minutes / R$25. —Note. — —Cacique de Ramos. R. Uranos 1326, Olaria. No metro adjacent. Count about 25 minutes by ride-hailing from Zona Sul / R$50. —Note. — —Weather. 28 °C, 15 % rain, partly sunny. This is the warm dry day. Monday brings 26 °C and 50 % rain; Tuesday 23 °C and 50 %; Wednesday 23 °C and 35 %; Thursday 22 °C and 55 %. Bring sunglasses for afternoon and a light layer for the late return. —Note. — —Ride-hailing. Sunday surge should be low. The Cacique de Ramos return from Olaria is the longest route; pre-order if you go there. Metro runs reduced Sunday hours, so plan ride-hailing for any late return. —Note. — —Safety. Copacabana Av. Atlântica is well-lit and busy through midnight. Around Pedra do Sal, stay with the roda crowd and ride back rather than walking side streets after the music ends. —Note.

07 Plan B

›Beco do Rato Sunday feijoada. R. Joaquim Silva 11, Lapa. Open 12h–21h for feijoada and afternoon roda. The Lapa option if Pedra do Sal is not on the route. ›Blue Note Rio brunch + calçadão. Av. Atlântica 1910. Sunday opening at 13h includes brunch before the 19h show. The calçadão and piano bar continue through the evening with free piano music. ›Samba da Feira at Praça Lima Barreto. Saturday’s all-day samba on R. do Lavradio is gone, but the Lavradio antiquário Sunday feira still runs until about 15h. Lunch on Mem de Sá afterward is the natural pivot. ›Nova Capela. Av. Mem de Sá 96, Lapa. The 1903 boteco with late kitchen and cabrito assado as the house dish. Good Sunday dinner option if the roda plan ends in Lapa.

08 Frequently Asked Questions

What is Amy Reggaehouse? Amy Reggaehouse is a project created in 2016 by the Bahian cantora Clariana Fróes, dedicated to releituras of the Amy Winehouse catalogue with arranjos that blend reggae, soul, jazz and Brazilian music. The project won The Winehouse Awards 2020 as the best Amy Winehouse tribute in the world. Clariana Fróes is a Salvador-born singer increasingly recognised in MPB; the project has toured Salvador, Belo Horizonte, São Luís and the Pelourinho circuit, and recorded its first audiovisual at the Sesc Casa do Comércio in Salvador in March 2026. Tonight’s show at Blue Note Rio (Sunday May 17, 2026 at 19h) is part of the post-recording tour. Is Pedra do Sal open on Sunday? Yes. Pedra do Sal runs its samba roda from Friday through Monday, with Sunday starting at 18h on the Largo João da Baiana / R. Argemiro Bulcão in the Saúde-Gamboa neighbourhood. Sunday is the second-busiest of the four roda nights (Monday is the legendary peak; Friday is the second-density night). Entry is free; food and drink come from barraca vendors on the cobblestones, cash only — bring small bills. The site was designated a Território Remanescente de Quilombo Urbano by the Fundação Cultural Palmares in 2005. Closest metro is Uruguaiana (Line 1) plus VLT to Parada dos Museus, or direct ride from Copacabana approximately R$25. Where is Cacique de Ramos and what’s the Sunday feijoada? Cacique de Ramos is the historical samba quadra at R. Uranos 1326 in Olaria, on the Zona Norte. The casa has been running Sunday rodas for decades and is where Zeca Pagodinho, Beth Carvalho, Arlindo Cruz and Jorge Aragão came up before becoming national figures. The roda starts every Sunday at 17h. On the third Sunday of each month, the casa runs the famous Feijoada do Cacique de Ramos starting at 13h with free entry — Sunday May 17, 2026 is the third Sunday, so the feijoada runs today. Ride from Zona Sul approximately 25 minutes / R$50; no metro adjacent. The audience is multi-generational and family-oriented, less tourist-heavy than the central Rio rodas. What time is Sunday samba at Bip Bip? Bip Bip’s Sunday samba roda starts at 19h. The bar’s standing programme runs Tuesday choro 20h, Wednesday bossa nova 20h, Thursday samba 21h, Sunday samba 19h; Friday and Saturday are open with rotating informal programming. Bip Bip occupies 18 square metres at R. Almirante Gonçalves 50 in Copacabana (since 1968) and runs no door, no cover, no waiter service — customers pull beer from the fridge and the bar runs on the honour system. Arrive early for any seat. The bar’s culture is strict: no clapping mid-song, no shouting, no photography during music. Metro Cardeal Arcoverde two minutes’ walk. What’s the Rio weather forecast for the week ahead? Sunday May 17 reaches 28 °C with 15% rain probability — partly sunny, the warmest day of the week ahead. Monday May 18 cools to 26 °C with 50% rain — the next system arriving. Tuesday May 19 cools further to 23 °C with 50% rain. Wednesday May 20 at 23 °C with 35% rain. Thursday May 21 at 22 °C with 55% rain. The dry pattern of last weekend is ending; Sunday is the last warm clear day before the system settles in for the working week. Plan indoor venues from tomorrow onward.

World.title: Healthcare Documents in Brazil: What Expats Should Keep Ready
World.content:
Key Facts —The core file: Foreigners should keep passport, CPF, insurance, prescriptions, allergies and vaccination records accessible. —The translation issue: Important medical history should be understandable to Brazilian doctors, especially in emergencies. —The prescription issue: Foreign prescriptions may not transfer cleanly to Brazilian pharmacies. —The insurance issue: Claims and reimbursements require documents, receipts and proof of care. —The practical rule: Build a digital and printed emergency file before it is needed.

Healthcare documents in Brazil are easy to ignore until a foreigner needs a doctor quickly. A small emergency file can save time, reduce confusion and make private insurance, appointments and pharmacy visits much easier.

What should be in the healthcare file?

Foreigners should keep copies of passport, visa or residence document, CPF, health-insurance card, emergency contacts, blood type if known, allergies, regular medications and key medical history.

Vaccination records and recent test results can also help. Families should keep separate files for each child and make sure both parents can access them.

Why prescriptions need planning

A medicine used abroad may have a different brand name, dosage or regulatory status in Brazil. Some prescriptions may need to be reissued by a Brazilian doctor.

Expats who depend on regular medication should bring enough supply for the transition period and schedule a local medical appointment early.

How should insurance documents be handled?

Private health plans and international insurers may require receipts, reports, invoices and proof of payment. These should be stored immediately after care, not searched for months later.

A simple folder on the phone and a printed backup can make emergencies and reimbursements less stressful.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do expats need vaccination records in Brazil?

They are useful, especially for children, schools, travel and medical appointments.

Will foreign prescriptions work in Brazil?

Not always. Some medications require a Brazilian prescription or local equivalent.

Should medical documents be translated?

Important conditions, allergies and medication lists should be available in Portuguese or in a format a Brazilian doctor can understand.

Connected Coverage

This guide belongs to our Living in Brazil cluster. Continue with our best places to live in Brazil, cost of living guide, private health insurance guide and first 48 hours in Brazil.

Sources

Reported by The Rio Times — Brazil relocation and Living in Brazil guide. Filed May 17, 2026.

World.title: São Paulo Daily Brief for Sunday, May 17, 2026
World.content:
A wet Sunday with the marquee Latin American opening of the year at MASP and the Z4 six-pointer at the Nilton Santos. CBF Copa do Brasil oitavas draw May 26; Virada Cultural May 23–24.

Sunday holds at 21°C with 53% rain risk, escalating into Monday at 65%. Tuesday clears to 20% rain but cools sharply to 18°C; Wednesday recovers to 20°C with only 15% rain. Waterproof layer plus warm mid-layer through Monday. Sunset 17h33.

This is part of The Rio Times’ daily Rio de Janeiro/São Paulo daily guide coverage for expats and the international community.

Sunday opens at 17°C in São Paulo with the high at 21°C and 53% rain, a cool wet day with sharper deterioration into Monday at 65% rain. Botafogo host Corinthians 16h at the Nilton Santos for Brasileirão Round 16 (Globo, Premiere) in a six-pointer between two clubs on 18 points fighting the Z4. Santos host Coritiba 11h Vila Belmiro (Premiere); RB Bragantino host Vitória 18h30 Nabi Abi Chedid (Premiere). Saturday’s results: Palmeiras drew 1–1 with Cruzeiro at the Arena Crefisa Barueri in heavy rain (Arroyo 11′, Felipe Anderson golaço 20’/1T; Felipe Anderson left injured in the posterior coxa), the third consecutive Brasileirão draw with the torcida booing at full-time; Fluminense beat São Paulo 2–1 at the Maracanã with Hulk presented to the crowd before kickoff. Today: Damián Ortega opens his first São Paulo institutional solo at MASP , free on Sundays.

03 What to See & Do CULTURE

TODAY’S PICK — MASP — AVENIDA PAULISTA Damián Ortega, Matéria e Energia — first São Paulo institutional solo, free Sunday The Damián Ortega retrospective at MASP opened Friday May 15 and runs through September 13. Sundays are free entry through the TIM partnership and rooms open at 10h, so this is the day to see it without the weekday queue. Curated by Adriano Pedrosa, Rodrigo Moura and Yudi Rafael, the show covers more than thirty years of work from the Mexico City artist (b. 1967), the most influential figure of the post-1990s Mexican generation that reshaped Latin American conceptual sculpture. After São Paulo, the show travels to the Centro Cultural La Moneda in Santiago (November 2026 to March 2027) in partnership with MALBA Buenos Aires. What to look for: Cosmic Thing (2002), the iconic exploded Volkswagen Beetle suspended in space; the photographic series; the tijolo and pedra works that map material as social and political diagram. The exhibition includes a set of pieces investigating Brazilian architecture made specifically for this iteration. Per Pedrosa in the catalogue, “Ortega’s practice converts the everyday object into a vector of social, economic and political narrative.” Where to go after: walk five minutes south on Avenida Paulista to the Itaú Cultural for Mestre Didi (free), then ten minutes east to the IMS Paulista for the rotating photography programme. Free Sundays and Tuesdays · MASP, Avenida Paulista 1578 · Tue/Thu/Fri/Sat/Sun 10h–18h · Wed 10h–20h.

THE CONTRASTING PLAY — PINACOTECA LUZ Pascale Marthine Tayou, Nocaute — for the painting-and-sculpture counterweight If MASP is the Mexican conceptual rigour, the Pinacoteca Luz is the Cameroonian sensorial maximalism, and they pair as a São Paulo art Sunday with the Estação da Luz at the centre. The Pascale Marthine Tayou retrospective Nocaute runs through August 2 across seven rooms on the first floor of the Pina Luz, the artist’s first institutional Brazilian show. Tayou (Yaoundé, b. 1966) crosses sculpture, painting and installation with materials drawn from West African market culture and European globalisation: cut crystal, cooking pots, plastic toys, raffia. The work is loud, theatrical, and unexpectedly funny. Combine route: MASP (10h–13h) → Avenida Paulista lunch → Linha 1 Azul metrô Paulista to Luz (15 min) → Pinacoteca (14h–18h). Linha Amarela Estação da República is the alternative. Tue–Sun 10h–18h · R$50 / R$25 meia · Praça da Luz 2.

TONIGHT, AFTER 19H Sunday samba spine and the Vila Madalena late-night route For Sunday samba: Sambinha do Casarão at Rua Aurora 391, Centro runs from 17h with the Vila Buarque rotation. Bar Brahma at the Avenida São João 677 corner runs the Sunday choro session 18h–22h, R$30 cover. For Vila Madalena: Lá da Venda at Rua Harmonia 161 runs the Sunday lunch-and-music programme until 19h with the rotating samba-pagode line-up; the streets around Aspicuelta and Mourato Coelho stay busy with the Sunday after-lunch crowd. For the more experimental Sunday option: Audio Rebel SP mirrors the Botafogo Rio venue at Rua Augusta 2840, Consolação with the experimental Sunday programme from 20h, R$25 antecipado. Casa de Francisca at Rua José Maria Lisboa 190, Jardim Paulista runs the Sunday jazz vespertino from 19h. For a quieter evening: SESC Pompeia runs the Sunday Lina Bo Bardi-designed-fábrica programme until 21h, with the open-air swimming pool and the deck on the top of the convivência tower at the original SESC. Free entry. Rua Clélia 93.

ALSO ON Pina Estação Macunaíma é Duwid (Gustavo Caboco curatorship) + Beatriz Milhazes, Tue–Sun 10h–18h · Pina Contemporânea Para Crianças in partnership with Haus der Kunst Munich · CCBB São Paulo rotating programme, free, Wed–Mon 9h–20h · Itaú Cultural Mestre Didi free + Ana Botafogo · IMS Paulista photography free · Museu da Imagem e do Som (MIS) · Parque Ibirapuera Sunday programme with Bienal Pavilion · Mercado Municipal Sunday lunch until 16h.

04 Getting Around TRANSPORT

METRÔ AND CET — SUNDAY Metrô SP runs Sunday hours 4h40–midnight across Linhas 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 15. Linha 1 Azul stations Paulista and Luz serve the MASP-Pinacoteca double afternoon. CPTM runs reduced Sunday timetable on Linhas 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13. Avenida Paulista closes to traffic Sunday 8h–17h for the Paulista Aberta programme — pedestrian and cyclist activities up to MASP and beyond. Rodízio is suspended Sundays. Roads for the matchday: Marginal Tietê and Pinheiros normal Sunday volumes 14h–18h flow toward the Nilton Santos for those driving up the Dutra. For Allianz Parque (no game Sunday), normal weekend volumes. Guarulhos (GRU) Sunday normal flow; Congonhas (CGH) reduced. Aeroporto Internacional Guarulhos confirmed normal operations after Saturday’s frente-fria-related delays.

05 Where to Eat FOOD

SUNDAY — LUNCH AND THE PAULISTA-LUZ ROUTE Avenida Paulista lunch: Casa Santo Antônio at Av. Paulista 2073 runs the Sunday-aberta menu from 11h30. Bráz Pizzaria at R. Sergipe 406, Higienópolis serves the Sunday lunch from 12h. For Luz post-Pinacoteca: Bar do Mané at Mercado Municipal R. Cantareira 306 runs the famous mortadella sandwich until 16h. Mocotó at Av. Nossa Senhora do Loreto 1100, Vila Medeiros (R$120) runs the buchada-and-feijoada Sunday until 17h. For Liberdade post-MASP: Aska at R. Galvão Bueno 466 runs Sunday from 11h30.

SUNDAY — DINNER Sunday dinner: D.O.M. (Atala) and A Casa do Porco (Janaína Torres) closed Sundays. Maní (Helena Rizzo R$320) closed Sunday. Tujá at R. Diogo Jácome 859, Moema runs Sunday 19h–23h. Tan Tan at R. Fradique Coutinho 235, Vila Madalena until 22h. Bar da Dona Onça at Edifício Copan R$95 until 22h Sunday.

06 Practical Info ESSENTIALS

SUNDAY SERVICES Bank branches closed Sunday; ATM and digital channels run continuously. Shopping centres operate 13h–21h Sunday (Shopping Iguatemi São Paulo, Cidade Jardim, Pátio Higienópolis, JK Iguatemi). The May 30 IRPF deadline is 13 days away. Pharmacies on plantão (Drogaria São Paulo, Drogasil, Pague Menos). Defesa Civil holds São Paulo on yellow alert through Monday given the 60%+ rain forecast; the Tietê remains in normal flow. Sunday street closures: Avenida Paulista 8h–17h (Paulista Aberta).

07 Community & Lifestyle EXPAT LIFE

Sunday in São Paulo at 21°C with 53% rain: a museum Sunday. Avenida Paulista closed for the Paulista Aberta 8h–17h. Parque Ibirapuera open 5h–23h with the Sunday running, biking and yoga programme; Parque Burle Marx open. International community: Aliança Francesa SP Sunday film cycle; British Society São Paulo Sunday tennis at the Hebraica; Goethe-Institut weekend cinema. Hebraica SP Sunday programme.

08 Game Day SPORT

BOTAFOGO X CORINTHIANS — 16H NILTON SANTOS — GLOBO/PREMIERE Diniz’s Timão visit the Glorioso in a Z4 six-pointer Corinthians visit Botafogo at the Nilton Santos 16h for Brasileirão Round 16 (Globo, Premiere) with both clubs on 18 points fighting the Z4. Fernando Diniz’s probable XI: Hugo Souza; Matheuzinho, André Ramalho, Gustavo Henrique, Bidu; Raniele, André, Bidon, Garro; Lingard, Yuri Alberto. Diniz holds a 3-4-11 record across 18 matches against Botafogo, the worst of his career against any single club. Saturday’s Palmeiras 1–1 Cruzeiro at the Arena Crefisa Barueri came in heavy rain (Arroyo 11′, Felipe Anderson golaço 20’/1T). Palmeiras stay top on 35 points with a third consecutive Brasileirão draw; the torcida booed at full-time. Felipe Anderson left injured in the posterior coxa esquerda (the eighth-minute substitution was Ramón Sosa, tornozelo), interrupting his best phase since arriving in 2024. Abel Ferreira returned from STJD suspension. Public 27,657, renda R$903,506.

SUNDAY ALSO — SANTOS, BRAGANTINO, ATHLETICO X FLAMENGO Santos x Coritiba 11h; Bragantino x Vitória 18h30; Ancelotti at Athletico x Flamengo Santos host Coritiba 11h Vila Belmiro (Premiere) in the early-morning slot. RB Bragantino host Vitória 18h30 Nabi Abi Chedid (Premiere). The Sunday closer is Athletico-PR x Flamengo 19h30 Arena da Baixada (Premiere, SporTV) with Carlo Ancelotti in the stands ahead of Monday’s Brazil World Cup pre-list announcement at the Museu do Amanhã. Seven Flamengo names watched: Danilo, Léo Pereira, Alex Sandro, Samuel Lino, Pedro, Léo Ortiz and Lucas Paquetá. Saturday: Fluminense 2–1 São Paulo at the Maracanã (John Kennedy 18’/1T, Canobbio 44’/1T; Dória 33’/2T), Hulk presented before kickoff. Internacional thrashed Vasco 4–1 at the Beira-Rio with Carbonero twice and Cuesta sent off late. São Paulo Tuesday: Millonarios at the Morumbis 21h30 (Sul-Americana R5); Palmeiras Tuesday: Cerro Porteño at the Allianz Parque 21h30 (Libertadores R5).

09 Business & Markets FINANCE

Friday closed the fifth consecutive losing week for the Ibovespa. The index fell 0.61% to 177,283.83 points; the week accumulated a 3.71% loss on R$32.2 billion volume. The dollar surged 1.59% to R$5.0664, back above R$5.00 with the week +3.48% (YTD -7.70%). Risk-off was driven by Trump’s Iran-patience comments, rising US Treasury yields on inflation concerns, the Dow falling 1.07% and Nasdaq 1.54%, plus a new Intercept Brasil reportage on the Flávio Bolsonaro–Vorcaro relationship that landed mid-afternoon. Per Nomad’s Paula Zogbi, the session “consolidates a strongly risk-off scenario with aggressive global asset repricing.” Sunday is a market-closed day. Monday opens with Asian markets digesting the US risk-off, the Trump-Iran tone and the weekend Brazilian political news cycle. Key data this week: April retail sales Tuesday, midweek IGP-10 inflation print, Friday IBC-Br activity proxy for March. The Petrobras Q1 reportage continues to ripple through the local energy book. The Selic remains at 14.75%; terminal forecasts spread BTG/ASA 13.00% to SulAmérica 14.00% for end-2026. Next Copom meeting June 17–18. April IPCA at 0.67% (12-month 4.39%) is near the BCB 4.5% upper-target band.

10 Plan Ahead COMING UP

THIS WEEK Mon May 18: Ancelotti announces Brazil World Cup 26-name squad 18h at Museu do Amanhã. Rodízio returns SP: plates 1–2. Tue May 19: Palmeiras x Cerro Porteño 21h30 Allianz Parque (Libertadores R5); São Paulo x Millonarios 21h30 Morumbis (Sul-Americana R5). COMING UP May 20: Corinthians x Platense 21h30 Neo Química Arena (Sul-Americana R5). May 23–24: Virada Cultural across São Paulo, MASP open 24 hours. May 26: CBF Copa do Brasil oitavas draw. May 23: Flamengo x Palmeiras 21h Maracanã (R17 marquee). May 30: 2025 IRPF deadline. Jun 17–18: Next Copom meeting.

11 Frequently Asked Questions FAQ

Where can I see Damián Ortega in São Paulo in May 2026?

The Damián Ortega retrospective Matéria e Energia opened Friday May 15 at MASP (Av. Paulista 1578) and runs through September 13, 2026. Sundays are free entry through the TIM partnership. Curated by Adriano Pedrosa, Rodrigo Moura and Yudi Rafael, this is the first São Paulo institutional solo for Ortega (b. Mexico City 1967) and covers more than thirty years of work. After São Paulo, the show travels to Centro Cultural La Moneda in Santiago, in partnership with MALBA Buenos Aires. Tue/Thu/Fri/Sat/Sun 10h–18h; Wed 10h–20h.

What time is Botafogo vs Corinthians on May 17?

World.title: Rio de Janeiro Daily Brief for Sunday, May 17, 2026
World.content:
A warm Sunday with the Brasileirão R16 closer, the city’s biggest samba festival of the autumn at Marina da Glória, and the eve of Ancelotti’s Brazil World Cup pre-list announcement at the Museu do Amanhã.

Sunday is the warmest day of the run at 28°C with only 20% rain, perfect beach conditions on the last clean window before Monday’s sharp shift to 60% rain. Tuesday cools to 23°C with 35% rain; Wednesday recovers slightly to 24°C. Light cottons for the day, full waterproof from Monday morning. Sunset 17h39.

This is part of The Rio Times’ daily Rio de Janeiro/São Paulo daily guide coverage for expats and the international community.

Sunday opens at 21°C in Rio with the high at 28°C and 20% rain, the warmest day of the week before Monday’s 60% rain shift. Athletico-PR host Flamengo 19h30 at the Arena da Baixada for Brasileirão Round 16 (Premiere, SporTV), with Carlo Ancelotti watching from the stands a day before Monday’s Brazil World Cup pre-list announcement at the Museu do Amanhã. Botafogo host Corinthians 16h Nilton Santos (Globo, Premiere) in a six-pointer between two clubs fighting the Z4. Fluminense beat São Paulo 2–1 Saturday at the Maracanã (John Kennedy and Canobbio in the first half, Dória pulled one back), climbing to 30 points and equaling Flamengo’s tally. Vasco were thrashed 4–1 by Internacional at the Beira-Rio (Carbonero scored twice and assisted twice; Cuesta sent off). Today: Capital do Samba Sunday at Marina da Glória with Raça Negra, Ferrugem, and Sorriso Maroto.

03 What to See & Do CULTURE

TODAY’S PICK — MAM RIO — PARQUE DO FLAMENGO Hélio Oiticica permanent + Rubem Valentim — the strongest Sunday in town After two weeks of No Martins at the MAR as the Today’s Pick, Sunday rotates the lead to the MAM Rio. Affonso Eduardo Reidy’s 1958 modernist building at the Aterro do Flamengo holds, year-in-year-out, the strongest single permanent gallery of twentieth-century Brazilian art on display anywhere: the Hélio Oiticica room, with the Parangolés, Bólides, and key Metaesquemas. Combine that with the Rubem Valentim retrospective currently on the upper floor and you have the canon-in-one-afternoon argument. Valentim was the Bahian who translated Candomblé iconography into geometric abstraction in the 1960s; the late paintings hold their own next to Tarsila and Volpi without straining. What to look for: in the Oiticica room, the small Metaesquemas on paper from 1957–58 — the moment when the artist breaks free of the European geometric grid and starts building the Brazilian one. In Valentim, the late Emblemas series. Per Adriano Pedrosa in the show catalogue, Valentim “completed the project of Brazilian abstraction by giving it a religious grammar.” Where to go after: walk south along the Aterro to Marina da Glória for Capital do Samba (15h onwards). Tue–Sun 10h–18h · R$14 / R$7 meia · Av. Infante Dom Henrique 85.

THE CONTRASTING PLAY — IMS GÁVEA Instituto Moreira Salles — for the photographic counterweight If MAM Rio is the painting canon, IMS Gávea is the photography canon, and they pair as an Aterro-to-Gávea Sunday afternoon. The IMS holds permanent and rotating exhibitions from one of the most important photography collections in South America, drawn from the Moreira Salles family’s six-decade-long acquisition project: Marc Ferrez’s 19th-century Rio panoramas, Pierre Verger’s Bahia of the 1940s, the Claudia Andujar Yanomami archive, and the contemporary rotation that currently includes a Letícia Parente video installation in the gardens. The Modernist house by Olavo Redig de Campos and Roberto Burle Marx alone is worth the visit. Free Sunday with the music programme starting 17h in the gardens. Combine route: MAM Rio (11h–13h) → Aterro lunch → Uber/taxi to Gávea (20 min) → IMS (14h–18h, music in the gardens 17h). Tue–Sun 11h–20h · Free · Rua Marquês de São Vicente 476.

TONIGHT, AFTER 19H Capital do Samba RJ — five sets at Marina da Glória The Sunday pick is Capital do Samba RJ at Marina da Glória, the fifth edition of the city’s biggest samba-and-pagode festival, from 15h. Sunday line-up: Raça Negra, Ferrugem, Sorriso Maroto, Menos é Mais, and Samba 90 Graus (with Netinho, Chrigor and Márcio Art). The setting is the open-air Marina da Glória with the Guanabara light through the afternoon and the Pão de Açúcar in the sightline; the festival has become one of the autumn-season anchors of the carioca calendar. Ingresse tickets in three sectors: Arena, Front Open Beer (cerveja and water), and Full Open Bar (premium with whisky, gin, vodka). Av. Infante Dom Henrique s/n, Glória. Sunday samba spine, for those wanting the smaller-room option: Sambinha do Mirante do Arvrão at the Vidigal mirante from 16h is the long-running open-air roda with Pão de Açúcar and Ipanema sightlines, and Samba do JB at the Jardim Botânico runs from 21h30 (Cozinha Arrumada + Roda do Firma + 1h open beer). The Pedra do Sal Sunday roda at Largo João da Baiana stays open in Saúde from 19h. For the post-show indoor option: Audio Rebel at Rua Visconde Silva 55, Botafogo runs the Sunday experimental programme from 20h, R$25 antecipado. Comuna at Rua Sorocaba 585, Botafogo stays open late.

ALSO ON MAR No Martins free Sunday, Praça Mauá 5, Tue/Sat free + 2nd-Sun-month · CCBB Rio Yoshitaka Amano free, Wed–Mon 9h–20h · Paço Imperial Constelações 40 anos, free, Tue–Sun 12h–18h · Casa França-Brasil photography, free · Museu do Amanhã Tue–Sun, paid, Praça Mauá 1 · Roda do Theo Bial Praça XV Sunday 14h, free · Cinemateca do MAM Sunday programme · Boulevard Olímpico Sunday feira and street performers.

04 Getting Around TRANSPORT

METRÔRIO — SUNDAY WITH NILTON SANTOS MATCHDAY MetrôRio runs Sunday hours 7h–23h on both lines. Linha 2 Estação Engenho de Dentro is the closest stop to the Nilton Santos for Botafogo x Corinthians 16h kickoff (heavy flows 13h30 inbound, 18h30 outbound). The VLT runs reduced Sunday timetable; VLT Parada dos Museus serves the MAR-Praça Mauá circuit and the Boulevard Olímpico. Rodízio is not in force in the city of Rio de Janeiro. Beaches: Posto 9 Ipanema and Posto 5 Copacabana run full Sunday rotation 7h–19h with lifeguards. Avenida Atlântica closes to traffic Sunday 7h–18h for the cyclists-and-walkers programme; the Aterro do Flamengo follows the same closure. Praia de Copacabana hosts the Sunday open-air market. Galeão (GIG) and Santos Dumont normal Sunday volumes. The Marina da Glória for Capital do Samba: arrive by Uber or VLT Antônio Carlos and walk.

05 Where to Eat FOOD

SUNDAY — LUNCH AND BEACH Sunday lunch in Ipanema: Garota de Ipanema at Rua Vinícius de Moraes 49 runs the picanha clássica from 12h. Cervantes at Av. Prado Júnior 335, Copacabana runs the sandwich with pineapple from 12h. For Aterro pre-MAM Rio: Aprazível (R. Aprazível 62, Santa Teresa) serves the Sunday lunch from 12h with views. Sushi Leblon (R. Dias Ferreira 256) runs Sunday from 13h. For Marina da Glória pre-Capital do Samba: Confeitaria Colombo at Praça Mauá 11 runs Sunday 9h–18h.

SUNDAY — DINNER Sunday dinner: Lasai (Rafa Costa e Silva) closed Sundays. Mocotó RJ at R. Coronel Souza Franco 162, Tijuca runs Sunday. Aconchego Carioca at R. Pereira de Almeida 11, Praça da Bandeira runs the bolinho-de-feijoada Sunday lunch and dinner. Zazá Bistrô Tropical at R. Joana Angélica 40, Ipanema until 23h.

06 Practical Info ESSENTIALS

SUNDAY SERVICES Bank branches closed Sunday; ATM and digital channels run continuously. Shopping centres operate 13h–21h Sunday (BarraShopping, Rio Sul, Shopping Leblon, Village Mall). The May 30 IRPF deadline is 13 days away. Pharmacies on plantão. The Praça XV ferry to Niterói runs reduced Sunday timetable; Paquetá-Praça XV runs full. Defesa Civil holds the city on normal status with no weather alerts. Sunday street closures: Avenida Atlântica and Aterro do Flamengo open to pedestrians 7h–18h.

07 Community & Lifestyle EXPAT LIFE

Sunday in Rio at 28°C with 20% rain: the warmest day of the week. Posto 9 Ipanema, Posto 5 Copacabana, and Posto 12 Leblon all active with full lifeguard staffing 7h–19h. Avenida Atlântica closed to traffic Sunday 7h–18h for the cycle-and-walk programme. The Aterro do Flamengo runs the same closure. Lagoa Rodrigo de Freitas 7.2 km perimeter open. Parque Lage 8h–17h. International community: Aliança Francesa Sunday film cycle; British Society Athletic Club Sunday tennis.

08 Game Day SPORT

ATHLETICO-PR X FLAMENGO — 19H30 BAIXADA — ANCELOTTI WATCHING Jardim’s Flamengo with Paquetá back; Carlo Ancelotti in the stands Athletico-PR host Flamengo at the Arena da Baixada Sunday 19h30 for Brasileirão Round 16 (Premiere, SporTV). Carlo Ancelotti will be in the stands a day before Monday’s Brazil World Cup pre-list announcement, with seven Flamengo names in the frame: Danilo, Léo Pereira, Alex Sandro, Samuel Lino, Pedro, Léo Ortiz, and Lucas Paquetá. Paquetá returns from a left-thigh injury. Flamengo desfalques: Erick Pulgar, Gonzalo Plata, Luiz Araújo did not travel; De La Cruz doesn’t play on synthetic. Leonardo Jardim’s Rubro-Negro sit second on 30 points (tied with Fluminense). Odair Hellmann’s Athletico are fifth on 23 points with the best home record in the league; they advanced in the Copa do Brasil mid-week on penalties over Atlético-GO. Athletico desfalques: Terán, Luiz Gustavo, Julimar (injured), Portilla (suspended).

BOTAFOGO X CORINTHIANS — 16H NILTON SANTOS — Z4 SIX-POINTER Both clubs on 18 points; both clubs in crisis Botafogo host Corinthians at the Nilton Santos Sunday 16h (Globo, Premiere) in a six-pointer between two clubs fighting the Z4 with the same 18 points. Franclim Carvalho’s Botafogo sit 14th and have not won a Brasileirão match in nearly a month; Thursday’s 2–0 loss to Chapecoense eliminated them from the Copa do Brasil. This is Alexander Barboza’s last Botafogo match before joining Palmeiras. Fernando Diniz’s Corinthians sit 16th and need a result to keep climbing. Saturday’s main results: Fluminense 2–1 São Paulo at the Maracanã (John Kennedy 18’/1T, Canobbio 44’/1T; Dória 33’/2T), Hulk officially presented before kickoff. Internacional thrashed Vasco 4–1 at the Beira-Rio with Carbonero scoring twice and assisting twice; Cuesta sent off late. Vasco dropped to 11th.

09 Business & Markets FINANCE

Friday closed the fifth consecutive losing week for the Ibovespa. The index fell 0.61% to 177,283.83 points; the week accumulated a 3.71% loss on R$32.2 billion volume. The dollar surged 1.59% to R$5.0664, back above R$5.00, with the week +3.48% (YTD -7.70%). Risk-off was driven by Trump’s Iran-patience comments, rising US Treasury yields on inflation concerns, the Dow falling 1.07% and Nasdaq 1.54%, plus a new Intercept Brasil reportage on the Flávio Bolsonaro–Vorcaro relationship that landed mid-afternoon. Per Nomad’s Paula Zogbi, the session “consolidates a strongly risk-off scenario with aggressive global asset repricing.” Sunday is a market-closed day. Monday opens with Asian markets digesting the US risk-off, the Trump-Iran tone, and the weekend Brazilian political news cycle. Key data this week: April retail sales Tuesday, midweek IGP-10 inflation print, Friday IBC-Br activity proxy for March. The Selic remains at 14.75%; terminal forecasts spread BTG/ASA 13.00% to SulAmérica 14.00% for end-2026. The next Copom meeting is June 17–18. April IPCA at 0.67% (12-month 4.39%) is near the BCB 4.5% upper-target band. The Prisma Fiscal report Thursday improved 2026 primary deficit forecast to R$57.8bn.

World.title: Bringing Pets to Brazil: What Expats Need to Know Before Flying
World.content:
Key Facts —The core requirement: Pets need documentation, identification and health compliance before they can enter Brazil legally. —The timing issue: Vaccines, certificates and airline approvals must be handled before travel day, not at the airport. —The housing issue: Apartment buildings and landlords may have pet rules that matter as much as the import paperwork. —The cost issue: Airline fees, crates, vet checks, translations and local setup costs should be budgeted separately. —The practical rule: Confirm the airline, apartment and destination vet before buying the ticket.

Bringing pets to Brazil is not difficult when the move is planned early. The risk is treating the animal as luggage instead of as a separate relocation project with documents, airline rules, housing restrictions and veterinary care.

What documents do pets need to enter Brazil?

Bringing pets to Brazil usually requires a valid health certificate, vaccination proof and compliance with Brazilian agricultural-health rules. Requirements can change, so foreign residents should verify the current rules with Brazilian authorities and the airline before departure.

Dogs and cats are the most common cases. Other animals may face different restrictions or additional controls. The safest approach is to ask a licensed vet in the departure country to prepare the travel file and then confirm it against Brazil’s official guidance.

Why airline rules matter as much as government rules

Even when the paperwork is correct, the airline can still decide whether the pet travels in cabin, as checked baggage or as cargo. Size, breed, crate type, aircraft model and route all matter.

Brachycephalic breeds, heat exposure and long connections require special caution. Brazil can be hot on arrival, and delays can turn a normal trip into a stressful animal-welfare problem.

What should expats check after arrival?

New arrivals should identify a local veterinarian, confirm emergency clinics and register the pet with the building or landlord if required. In large Brazilian cities, high-quality private veterinary care is available, but location matters.

Pet shops, grooming, dog walkers and boarding services are common in wealthier districts. In smaller cities, services may be cheaper but less internationalized.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can foreigners bring dogs and cats to Brazil?

Yes. Dogs and cats can generally enter Brazil when documentation, vaccination and health-certificate requirements are met.

Should I choose the apartment before bringing a pet?

Yes. Some buildings and landlords restrict pets, size or breed. Housing should be confirmed before the animal travels.

Is pet care expensive in Brazil?

Routine care can be reasonable, but emergency care, imported food, special medication and boarding can add meaningful monthly cost.

World.title: Learning Portuguese in Brazil: The Expat Shortcut to a Better Life
World.content:
Key Facts —The biggest lever: Portuguese improves almost every part of expat life in Brazil faster than any app, service or shortcut. —The first target: New arrivals should learn survival Portuguese for housing, transport, pharmacies, banks and healthcare before chasing fluency. —The social effect: Even imperfect Portuguese changes how Brazilians respond and how quickly foreigners build trust. —The work effect: Career and business options expand sharply when foreigners can handle meetings, contracts and informal conversations. —The practical rule: Study daily, speak badly early and treat mistakes as part of the relocation process.

Learning Portuguese in Brazil is not optional for foreigners who want a real life rather than a protected bubble. English helps in some hotels, startups and elite services, but Portuguese is what turns Brazil from a beautiful place into a manageable home.

What Portuguese should expats learn first?

The first goal is not literary Portuguese. It is functional Portuguese. New arrivals need phrases for renting, ordering food, calling ride-hailing drivers, explaining health problems, dealing with pharmacies and asking for help.

Pronunciation matters because Brazilian Portuguese is not Spanish with different spelling. Foreigners who invest early in sounds, rhythm and listening comprehension progress faster in real conversations.

How should foreigners study in Brazil?

The best method combines structured lessons with daily exposure. A tutor can explain grammar and correction, while shops, taxis, gyms and cafés provide repetition.

A realistic routine is 30 to 45 minutes of study each day plus one deliberate conversation task. The task can be simple: ask for a product, call a building porter, schedule an appointment or explain a delivery problem.

Where Portuguese matters most

Portuguese matters most when something goes wrong. Healthcare, banking, repairs, police reports, condominium rules, school meetings and bureaucracy all become easier when the foreigner can explain the issue clearly.

It also changes social life. Brazilians are often generous with foreigners who try, but they will not always switch to English. The effort itself builds goodwill.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I live in Brazil with only English?

Yes, but daily life becomes narrower and more expensive. Portuguese makes housing, healthcare, bureaucracy and friendships much easier.

How long does it take to learn Portuguese in Brazil?

Basic survival Portuguese can develop in a few months with daily practice. Professional fluency takes much longer.

Is Brazilian Portuguese very different from European Portuguese?

Yes. Pronunciation, vocabulary and rhythm differ. Expats in Brazil should focus on Brazilian Portuguese from the start.
